proposition.claim:
Recorded check: The positive-entropy leading resonance is false for the specified scalar operator

Dimension and group. V=R^2 satisfies d>1. A closed genus at least two oriented hyperbolic surface has faithful holonomy lift avoiding -I because the Euler class is even; projection is injective, hence the subgroup is torsion-free. Projective Anosov and irreducibility. Cocompact Fuchsian translation lengths control stable word length and the two eigenvalue moduli give the gap. No real invariant line exists for this non-elementary lattice. Assigned domain and basic set. The full RP^1 limit set makes every transverse pair admissible, so M=K=Gamma-bar\PSL(2,R), a compact manifold. This compact case is expressly admitted on source p.3. Potential and operator. U=0 is smooth and compactly supported on the compact manifold, and A=-X is exactly the scalar operator specified. Resolvent and entropy. Contact volume is finite and invariant; composition by the flow is unitary. The right-half-plane resolvent integral is analytic. The flow is the positive constant time rescaling of a compact hyperbolic geodesic flow and has h>0.

Recorded check: The allowed cyclic case has two periodic components and a double zeta pole

Group range. Infinite cyclic is non-trivial, torsion-free, finitely generated and hyperbolic; non-elementarity is not in these literal statements. Gap and limit maps. Stable word length of g^n is |n| and eigenvalue-log gap is 2|n|log(2), satisfying c=c'=log(2). The primal maps are e1,e2 and the corresponding dual maps are e2*,e1*, giving cross-pair transversality. Periodic identification. Both ordered endpoint pairs remain distinct under this abelian action. Each real fiber quotients by translation of absolute size log(2). Both g and g^(-1) are primitive and nonconjugate. One-dimensional application. The positive projective interval is properly strictly convex under the stated definition, its Hilbert quotient is compact, and its unit sphere bundle consists of the two oriented periodic circles.

Recorded check: A relative sign sends the pseudo-hyperbolic map outside its target

Permitted signature. p=2,q=0 is within the stated range. Unit spacelike tangent domain. The explicit x,v have B(x,x)=-1, B(v,v)=1 and B(x,v)=0. Target and quotient. The target requires positive B(v1,v2); both entries have one common projective scaling, so the negative pairing cannot be removed by an allowed common rescaling.

Recorded check: The printed residue is the negative projector and the initial half-plane ignores the potential

Compact admissible example. All geometric and group hypotheses are the same verified ones as P001. Allowed potential. The real constant c>0 is smooth; its support is compact because the ambient manifold is compact. Exact operator convention. The computation uses precisely the stated A=-X+U and (A-lambda)^(-1), on its invariant constants.

Recorded check: The local-product point need not belong to the basic set for an arbitrary ambient base point

Section 4 group hypotheses. A classical torsion-free Schottky group is non-elementary, irreducible in the standard representation, convex cocompact and projective Anosov. Base point and neighborhoods. Take x in K and choose y in the local stable leaf inside the prescribed ambient ball and domain; openness and the nowhere dense Cantor endpoint set permit this for every sufficiently small radius. Ambient plaque and uniqueness. The analytic ambient stable and central-unstable plaques are defined at y. It belongs to both Ws(x) and Wcu(y); their local-product intersection is unique.

repair.content:
Specify the appropriate differential-form degree, any orientation twist, pairing and open-system extension; or change the scalar potential and prove the altered pressure/regularity claims. A global resolvent sign change cannot move poles. A merely Holder conjugacy does not automatically transport wavefront-defined distribution products.

Add non-elementarity where used, or state the cyclic two-orbit case separately. Retain needed irreducibility/dimension qualifiers in applications.

Use [x+v:v-x] with the consistent inverse [v1-v2:v1+v2] and common unit normalization. The geodesic equations then give the required e^t/e^(-t) scaling.

Use -Res(A-lambda)^(-1), or (lambda-A)^(-1); start in Re(lambda)>sup Re(U) with invariant volume. For P=-iX use lambda=-iz, so Re(lambda)=Im(z), and invoke the open-system counting statements with their hypotheses.

Require y in K intersected with the small ball. Clarify that item (5) parallel transport is along the leaf where it was defined.
